Years 11–13 Mathematics
and Statistics

Learning expectations
Through Mathematics and Statistics students develop mathematical and statistical reasoning,
problem-solving, data literacy, and quantitative and qualitative analysis. Students are taught how to
represent, analyse, and solve problems using numerical, algebraic, graphical, geometric,
statistical, and computational methods.

The learning area supports students to think critically, evaluate evidence, communicate concepts
precisely, and apply mathematics and statistics across a wide range of authentic contexts using
evidence.


Key features of the refreshed learning area
•   Clear progression from Years 9–10 through to advanced specialist mathematics and statistics
    pathways.
•   Strong emphasis on mathematical reasoning, problem-solving, and the practical application of
    knowledge.
•   Explicit teaching of disciplinary writing and communication, helping students explain and justify
    mathematical and statistical thinking.
•   Greater visibility of financial mathematics, statistical literacy, data science, modelling, and data-
    informed decision-making.
•   Purpose-built pathways that support students with different interests, strengths, and future
    aspirations.
•   Strong connections between theory and authentic real-world contexts, including industry,
    technology, science, engineering, economics, and data-rich environments.


Subjects
Subjects within the Mathematics and Statistics learning area:

•   Year 11 Mathematics and Statistics
•   Years 12–13 Mathematics
•   Years 12–13 Mathematical and Statistical Modelling
•   Year 13 Statistics and Data Science
•   Year 13 Further Mathematics.

Learning and pathways

Year 11 Mathematics and Statistics
Students are taught to apply foundational mathematical knowledge and further develop number,
algebra, measurement, geometry, probability, and statistics concepts and application expertise.
They apply mathematical principles and procedures to solve problems, interpret information, and
model situations. Students use numerical, algebraic, graphical, and geometric methods to
investigate relationships, recognise patterns, and communicate mathematical ideas using
appropriate representations.

Strands

Year 11 Mathematics is organised into four strands:

•   Number and Algebra
•   Measurement and Geometry
•   Statistics and Probability
•   Disciplinary Writing.

Pathways

Year 11 Mathematics and Statistics provides the foundation for all senior mathematics and
statistics pathways. Students may choose to take both Year 12 Mathematics and Year 12
Mathematical and Statistical Modelling subjects following Year 11, as these subjects have been
designed as separate subjects.




Year 11 Mathematics and Statistics supports learning across science, technology, commerce,
health, social sciences, and many other learning areas. It contributes to pathways in fields such as
architecture, engineering, finance, logistics, education, and technology.

Years 12–13 Mathematics
Students are taught to apply mathematical knowledge and further develop numeric, algebraic,
trigonometric, and mathematical statistics concepts and application expertise. They apply
principles and procedures to solve problems, investigate relationships, and communicate
mathematical ideas using appropriate representations.

Strands

Years 12–13 Mathematics is organised into three strands:
•   Algebra and Geometry
•   Calculus
•   Mathematical Statistics.

Pathways

Year 12 Mathematics provides a pathway to all Year 13 Mathematics and Statistics subjects. The
suggested learning area pathway is for students to progress from Year 12 Mathematics to Year 13
Mathematics or Year 13 Further Mathematics.




This subject prepares students for tertiary study and careers in mathematics, engineering,
computer science, physics, finance, chemistry, technology, and related STEM fields.


Years 12–13 Mathematical and Statistical Modelling
Students are taught mathematical, statistical, and probabilistic concepts, representations, and
methods. They explore context-specific information to analyse problems, identify patterns and
relationships, and develop solutions in both tangible and theoretical contexts.

Strands

Years 12–13 Mathematical and Statistical Modelling is organised into four strands:

•   Mathematical Modelling
•   Statistical Modelling
•   Probability Modelling
•   Disciplinary Writing.

Pathways

Year 12 Mathematical and Statistical Modelling provides a pathway to all Year 13 Mathematics and
Statistics subjects. The suggested pathway is for students to progress from Year 12 Mathematical
and Statistical Modelling to Year 13 Mathematical and Statistical Modelling or Year 13 Statistics
and Data Science.




This subject supports pathways in business, economics, environmental science, health sciences,
planning, operations research, data analytics, and a wide range of applied mathematical fields.


Year 13 Statistics and Data Science
Students are taught statistical and data concepts and methods to collect, analyse, and represent
data, and to use data to make informed decisions. They explore data collection, management, and
stewardship, alongside the interpretation of data and the justification of conclusions.

Strands

Year 13 Statistics and Data Science is organised into four strands:
•   Data Construction
•   Data Exploration
•   Decision Making from Data
•   Disciplinary Writing.

Pathways

Statistics and Data Science leads to pathways in data science, statistics, computer science,
business, psychology, accounting, health sciences, research, and other data-intensive professions.


Year 13 Further Mathematics
Students are taught to use logical reasoning, problem-solving, and mathematical skills to support
them to make informed and deliberate connections between theory and practice. They apply
concepts, techniques, and calculations to interpret and simplify mathematical problems.

Further Mathematics is to be taught alongside another Year 13 Mathematics and Statistics subject.

Strands

Year 13 Further Mathematics is organised into four strands:

•   Logic and Proof
•   Number Theory
•   Discrete Mathematics
•   Differential Equations.

Pathways

Further Mathematics supports pathways into advanced mathematics, physics, engineering,
computer science, software engineering, algorithm design, and related disciplines.


How to design a programme
The knowledge and practice statements within each element are related, but teachers may select
complementary statements from across the strands and elements to support coherence and depth
within a subject. Disciplinary communication is most effectively taught when integrated across the
teaching programme.


Connections to other learning areas
Mathematics and Statistics connects strongly with:

•   Science through measurement, modelling, experimentation, and data analysis
•   Technology through computational thinking, algorithms, coding, artificial intelligence, and data
    systems
•   Social Sciences through economics, business, demographics, and statistical investigations
•   Health and Physical Education through data interpretation, probability, measurement, and
    decision-making
•   English through disciplinary writing, communication of evidence, and evaluation of claims.
